newsitem.title: ITALY: TENNIS-CHAMPION MUSTER MAKES HAY IN THE SUNSHINE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-CHAMPION MUSTER MAKES HAY IN THE SUNSHINE.

text.p: Defending champion Thomas Muster allowed local wild card Marzio Martelli an hour in the sunshine at the Italian Open on Monday before tossing him aside.

The Austrian strongman with the piercing gaze gave the Italian a bit of a run around on centre court and then sent him on his way 6-3 6-2 in their first round match, Muster's 500th on clay in his career.
That was about the extent of the impression Martelli made on the muscular world number three, a man whose tough guy demeanour suggests he could chew bricks for breakfast if he wanted to.
Muster, the biggest seed in action on the opening day of the tournament, was Monday's first winner.
He did not mention Martelli once in a post-match news conference devoted almost entirely to Muster's new-found prowess on hardcourt and recent failures on clay.
"You cannot expect me to win every clay court tournament like I did two years ago," said the Austrian, who has won more clay court matches and titles than any other tour player.
In three tournaments on clay this year, Muster has not progressed beyond the round of 16.
The clay court Italian Open, a favourite venue where he has won for the past two years and three times in total, offers him the chance to reassert himself.
In Monte Carlo late last month he had a first round bye and then lost to France's Fabrice Santoro 6-2 7-6.
In Hamburg last week the 1995 French Open champion had another bye, beat Alex Radulescu of Germany and then went out to Moroccan Hicham Arazi 6-1 6-2.
Hardcourt has been a different story.
Muster won Dubai in February, The Lipton in March and was semifinalist at the Australian Open in January.
The Austrian, whose main goal is the French Open in two weeks, said he had problems on clay for a variety of reasons but was confident they were over.

"I had some health problems in the last couple of months and material-wise at the beginning of the clay court season. But they are now resolved and I am feeling physically better and better every day that I step on to the court," he said.
Muster did own up to motivation difficulties, saying that when one has won everything on clay it is hard not to concentrate on fresh challenges on other surfaces.

"If you have won all the big ones on clay and then you have success on other surfaces, which I have always wanted to do, then all your thoughts go to hardcourt and maybe you don't pay enough attention to what you have to do on clay," he said.
"Its definitely a different game that you play on hardcourt and you have to play in a very different style."
Muster was followed on court by Wimbledon champion Richard Krajicek. The fifth-seeded Dutchman was playing Diego Nargiso, another Italian wild card.
